title: Καλαμαράκια στο air fryer
description: Air-fryer squid with a light semolina and breadcrumb coating, based on the linked Argiro recipe.
reason_not_strict: Uses semolina and breadcrumbs or flour, plus parsley and olive oil.
equipment: COSORI Turbo Tower Pro Smart air fryer

ingredients.original: 2 tbsp finely ground breadcrumbs or flour

steps: Dry the squid thoroughly and cut it into rings.
Mix the coating ingredients and coat the squid lightly, shaking off the excess.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 C for 3 minutes.
Arrange the squid with space between pieces, spray lightly with olive oil, and cook for about 12 minutes at 200 C.
Mix once halfway through. For better crispness, cook in two batches.
notes: For a crisper result, cook in two batches. Source: https://www.argiro.gr/recipe/kalamarakia-sto-air-fryer/
recommendedReason: The source recipe is designed for air-fryer cooking.

oven.note: No oven method is specified in the source recipe.

airFryer.note: Cook in two batches when needed for better crispness.
instructions: Cook for about 12 minutes at 200 C.

blackstone.note: The source recipe is intended for the air fryer.

title: Γιουβαρλάκια αυγολέμονο
description: Greek beef-and-rice meatball soup finished with avgolemono, based on the linked Argiro recipe.
reason_not_strict: Includes rice, vegetables, cornflour and olive oil.

ingredients.item: medium dry onion, grated or very finely chopped
small celeriac, about 300 g, cut into small dice
a little finely chopped dill for finishing

steps: Soak the rice in plenty of water while preparing the other ingredients, then rinse and drain it well.
Combine the mince, egg, rice, onion, grated carrot, olive oil, herbs, salt and pepper. Knead thoroughly, then shape into walnut-sized meatballs.
Cut the soup vegetables into similarly sized small dice. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and saute the vegetables for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the hot water and bring to the boil. Add the meatballs, season, cover, reduce the heat and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.
At the end, reduce the heat to very low and let the vigorous boiling settle.
Mix the lemon juice with the cornflour. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then whisk in the yolks.
Temper the egg mixture with hot broth and the lemon-cornflour mixture, then return it gently to the pot without hard boiling.
Finish with a little finely chopped dill and adjust the seasoning.
notes: Cornflour is especially useful if the dish will be reheated, which should be done over very low heat, because it helps reduce the risk of the avgolemono splitting. Source: https://www.argiro.gr/recipe/giouvarlakia-avgolemono/

recommendedMethod.label: Stovetop saucepan
recommendedMethod.reason: The dish is a simmered soup finished with avgolemono and needs controlled stovetop heat.
instructions: Simmer the meatballs in the soup for 25 to 30 minutes.
Temper the avgolemono with hot broth.
Return it gently to the pot without hard boiling.

oven.note: The dish depends on stovetop simmering and tempering.

airFryer.note: An air fryer cannot produce the soup or avgolemono finish.

blackstone.note: A flat griddle is not suitable for this soup.

title: Μοσχάρι μπρεζέ με κόκκινο κρασί
description: Whole-piece slow-braised beef with a substantial fat cap, red wine, beef broth, carrot, celery and aromatics, adapted for about 1 kg of boneless beef.
reason_not_strict: Uses carrot, celery, onion, garlic, red wine, olive oil and herbs.
equipment: Dutch oven or heavy oven-safe casserole with tight-fitting lid

ingredients.item: boneless beef for slow cooking, whole piece with fat cap
ingredients.original: 1 kg boneless beef for slow cooking, whole piece with fat cap

ingredients.item: olive oil, using less if the beef renders plenty of fat
beef broth, added only as needed so the liquid reaches about halfway up the meat
freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.original: freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps: Preheat the oven to 160 C conventional or 150 C fan. Remove the beef from the vacuum pack and pat it very dry. Season well with salt and black pepper. Keep the piece whole. Trim only exceptionally thick or hard external fat; keep the main fat cap.

Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Put the beef in fat-side down first. Brown for about 4 to 5 minutes so the fat begins to render and develops good colour. Turn and brown the exposed meat side for about 3 to 4 minutes, then use tongs to brown the edges where practical. Add only as much olive oil as needed. Transfer the beef to a plate.
Add the onion, carrot and celery to the rendered fat in the pot. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften and colour. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until the wine is reduced by roughly half.

Return the beef to the pot with the fat cap facing upward. Add the bay leaf, thyme and rosemary. Add enough beef broth for the braising liquid to reach roughly halfway up the meat, at most about two-thirds. Do not automatically use all the broth.
Bring the liquid just to a gentle simmer on the stovetop. Cover tightly and transfer to the oven.

Braise for about 2 1/2 hours, then test the thickest part with a thin knife or fork. If there is clear resistance, continue cooking and check every 20 to 30 minutes. For a roughly 1 kg piece, expect around 3 to 3 1/2 hours in many cases. Tenderness, not the clock alone, determines doneness.
When a knife or fork enters with very little resistance, remove the beef and rest it for 15 to 20 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and herb stems. Skim excess visible fat from the braising liquid.

For a smoother, thicker sauce, blend the cooked vegetables into the braising liquid. Alternatively leave them intact. If the sauce is too thin, simmer it uncovered on the stovetop for 5 to 10 minutes to reduce before serving with the beef.
notes: Base recipe is 4 servings from about 1 kg raw boneless beef, approximately 250 g raw beef per serving. Numeric ingredient quantities scale automatically with the serving selector. Cooking time does not scale linearly with servings or meat weight; use tenderness as the endpoint. Adapted from Kelsey Nixon's Sunday Pot Roast (Food Network): https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/sunday-pot-roast-2125775. The source uses a 4 lb boneless chuck roast for 8 servings and the same core braising technique.
recommendedReason: For this whole, fatty slow-cooking cut, covered oven braising gives steady, even heat while the connective tissue softens.

oven.note: Use a covered Dutch oven or heavy oven-safe casserole.
instructions: Preheat to 160 C conventional or 150 C fan.
Braise covered until fork-tender, checking from 2 1/2 hours and typically allowing around 3 to 3 1/2 hours for a roughly 1 kg piece.
Rest the beef for 15 to 20 minutes before serving.

airFryer.note: This cut is intended for long, moist braising rather than dry air-fryer cooking.

blackstone.note: A flat griddle can brown the meat but cannot provide the covered moist braise required for the full recipe.
